---
title: "Under aridification the binding constraint is inflow, not storage: why building more dams is a supply-blind drought response"
author:
  - name: Francisco Zambrano Bigiarini
date: today
abstract: |
  Expanding reservoir storage is the reflexive policy response to intensifying drought, yet
  whether dams build resilience or merely mark where vulnerability already concentrates
  remains untested under sustained drying. We treat reservoir presence as a basin-level
  intervention across central Chile — 26 monitored reservoirs spanning the 2010–present
  megadrought — and estimate its effect on drought propagation and water-dependent land use
  using a national matched design (entropy balancing within Köppen × aridity strata; 21 of 24
  treated basins retained), doubly-robust matched ATT, forcing-conditioned
  difference-in-differences, and randomization inference. Across every operational pathway —
  meteorological-to-hydrological drought transmission, evapotranspiration buffering, and
  irrigated-area expansion — the treatment effect brackets zero once siting is matched out. A
  within-basin placebo comparing regulated downstream reaches against physically unregulated
  upstream reaches of the same dammed basins (15 of 21 basins) is decisive: the apparent
  national buffering signal (slope gap −0.18) is as strong upstream as downstream and
  collapses to ≈ −0.03 within climate region (p_perm = 0.39) — the signature of an
  aridity-gradient confound, not regulation. Refill efficiency is undiminished; instead
  storage shows a whole-band downshift, indicating the binding constraint is declining inflow,
  not storage capacity or operation. Reservoirs in Chile mark pre-existing,
  siting-determined vulnerability rather than make resilience — reframing storage expansion as
  a supply-blind response to aridification.
keywords:
  - reservoir effect
  - drought propagation
  - socio-hydrology
  - causal inference
  - megadrought
  - Chile
